technical.summary: CDW shows strong structural bullish alignment across moving averages and trend indicators, but overbought RSI(9) and lack of fresh crossover signals suggest caution on new long entries; better suited for existing position management or pullback entry.

fundamental.summary: CDW shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signals, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk within 84 days.

sentiment.summary: No actionable congressional signal; mixed market sentiment (neutral AAII, moderate greed) with no recent news data provides insufficient conviction for directional bias.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (186.6) indicates extreme market stress; earnings in 84 days adds event risk but is not imminent.

debate.key_bull_argument: Strong technical structure (price above all major MAs, supertrend bullish, Ichimoku above cloud) with positive squeeze provides a foundation for continuation if macro headwinds ease.
debate.key_bear_argument: Severe macro environment (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis levels), overbought RSI(9) at 74.6 with no fresh momentum signals, weak fundamentals (no insider conviction, high earnings risk in 84 days), and price near resistance (192.38) create unfavorable risk/reward for new long entry.

decision.entry_rationale: Technical structure is constructive with price above all major MAs and supertrend bullish, but overbought RSI(9) at 74.6 with no fresh crossover signals indicates momentum exhaustion at resistance.
decision.primary_risk: Severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis at 186.6) combined with high earnings risk in 84 days and weak fundamental conviction create asymmetric downside risk in a fragile market environment.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bearish bias despite technical strength
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding CDW position with 66 existing IT sector positions (19% of portfolio); adding concentration in high-volatility sector during macro crisis and VIX extremes is imprudent; manage existing position instead.
